Five terms written:

| Term | Grounding | σ fiber (recognizes) | Δ fiber (produces) | Formality |
|------|-----------|---------------------|---------------------|-----------|
| **communications-officer** | Shannon (1948), Barnard (1938) | Messages in transit, channel status, protocol violations | Delivered messages, routing tables, channel reports | F1 |
| **chief-medical-officer** | Shewhart (1931), Deming, Perrow (1984) | Health indicators, staleness, drift, capacity exhaustion | Health assessments, maintenance prescriptions, fitness certifications | F2 |
| **counselor** | Münsterberg (1913), Parsons (1951) | Capability gaps, role overload, compositional gaps | Fit assessments, training plans, reassignment recommendations | F1 |
| **tactical-officer** | Reason (1990), Buzan (1983), NIST/OWASP | Threats, vulnerabilities, posture gaps, active breaches | Threat assessments, posture recommendations, incident reports, security policies | F2 |
| **navigator** | Bowditch (1802), Dantzig (1947), Simon (1956) | Position vs goals, leverage opportunities, drift, dead ends | Route plans, position reports, leverage analyses, course corrections | F1 |

Each term defines the office positively, connects to the existing vocabulary (officer, officium, role, duty, office), grounds in real disciplinary theory with named sources, and distinguishes itself from adjacent offices already in the library. The two that need override authority (CMO and tactical) are F2; the three that are advisory are F1.
